overview: The Committee of the Whole reviewed FY 2023 budget proposals for the Department of Public Works, Fire, Finance, and Facilities, though discussions were preceded by a dispute regarding professional conduct and administrative transparency. The committee tabled the Information Technology and Veterans budgets pending further information.

items.title: Administrative Conduct and Budget Transparency
items.summary: Chief of Staff Nina Nazarian addressed alleged sexist and unprofessional behavior from council members in previous meetings, leading to a rebuttal regarding the administration's lack of communication and delayed budget documentation.

items.title: DPW - Water and Sewer
items.summary: The committee reviewed the Water and Sewer enterprise fund, focusing on indirect costs, lead service line inventory requirements, and the implementation of a citywide water meter replacement project.

items.title: Fire Department
items.summary: Chief John Friedman presented the Fire Department budget, detailing station renovations, recruitment challenges for academy slots, and the long-term goal of constructing a new headquarters.

items.title: DPW - Highway and Forestry
items.summary: Commissioner Tim McGivern discussed DPW operations, including rising trash removal contracts, the proposed hiring of two tree climbers for safety, and ongoing stump removal initiatives.

items.title: Parks Department
items.summary: The committee discussed the maintenance of athletic fields, dog leash enforcement on public property, and potential revenue generation through updated field rental permitting.

items.title: Engineering
items.summary: Discussions centered on major capital projects, including the Main and South Street intersection design and various grant-funded pedestrian safety improvements.

items.title: Cemetery
items.summary: The committee reviewed cemetery operations and the use of Community Preservation Act funds for the restoration of historic maintenance buildings.

items.title: Information Technology
items.summary: Approved a motion to table the IT budget until the administration provides a report on cybersecurity concerns and corrected financial spreadsheets.

items.title: Finance and Auditing
items.summary: Finance Director Bob Dickinson highlighted a structural deficit and the urgent need to transition from antiquated accounting software to a modern integrated system.

items.title: Building Department
items.summary: Discussion addressed the current vacancy of the Building Commissioner and the operational impact of being unable to issue certificates of occupancy without a licensed official.

items.title: Facilities and Grounds
items.summary: The committee examined the consolidated facilities budget and the difficulties in recruiting a director to oversee maintenance for municipal buildings like the new library.

items.title: Veterans
items.summary: Approved a motion to table the Veterans budget because a budget form was not provided and the subcommittee chair was absent.
